own_solution.law: Normal-incidence acoustic transmission: p_i = sqrt(2 Z1 I), p_t = 2 Z2/(Z1+Z2) * p_i, with Z = rho c
assumptions: intensity is the time-averaged intensity of a harmonic wave, I = p^2/(2 Z)

notes: Z1 = 1.2*343 = 411.6 Pa s/m; Z2 = 998*1482 = 1,479,036 Pa s/m. p_i = sqrt(2*411.6*0.012) = 3.14299 Pa; transmission factor 2Z2/(Z1+Z2) = 1.999444; p_t = 6.2842 Pa. With the first loudspeaker's intensity raised to 0.018 W/m^2: p_t = 6.2842*sqrt(1.5) = 7.6966 Pa. Frequency is a property of the wave that enters wavelength/displacement relations but not the normal-incidence pressure transmission coefficient (frequency-independent for lossless half-spaces), so C (one could also argue D-like irrelevance; I classify C as it belongs to the system). Second loudspeaker faces the boathouse wall and is taken as not contributing to the incident wave; earlier-trial changes leave no state. Numbered intensity sentences all use 0.006 W/m^2; TF89B and TBD48 carry no number (apparently numeral-free variants). Using I = p^2/(2Z) assumes a harmonic wave and amplitude (not rms) is asked, which is the standard reading.
